headline: Cut a circular list at the new tail
statement: Rotate a singly linked list to the right by k positions and return its new head. An empty list is allowed. Reuse original nodes without changing their values.
intuition: Rotating by the list length changes nothing, so reduce k modulo n. The last k nodes become the front. Connect the old tail to the old head, walk to the node just before the new head, and break that one link.
approach: Handle an empty or singleton list.
Find the length and old tail, then reduce k modulo length.
Return unchanged for zero effective rotation.
Join tail to head, advance length-k-1 links to the new tail, and break the circle.
correctness: The new tail is the last node of the original prefix of length n-k. Its successor is the first node of the original suffix. Closing the old tail-to-head edge concatenates suffix and prefix; cutting after the new tail preserves every node once in the required order.
bruteForce: Move the tail to the front k times, finding the tail on each pass: O(nk). Modulo and one cut avoid repeated traversals.

complexity.explanation: Two scans locate the old and new tails; existing nodes are reused.

pitfalls: Zero-length input must be handled before modulo.
